title: Provisioning records — shared definitions (design draft 0.1.0)
description: Definitions shared by the module's record schemas. Every record kind here is a content-addressed Novae Linguae artifact: the `hash` is BLAKE3-256 over the JCS-canonical record with `hash` (and, for signed kinds, `signature`) removed, rendered as `<prefix>_<64 hex>` (spec/canonical-serialization.md). The module proposes ten new address prefixes — kind, dish, rcp, needs, prof, plate, inst, rcpt, patt, stmt — as an additive extension of the prefix vocabulary (spec/README.md, Content-address format); until that extension lands in spec/, these records live in the module and are checked by the module's design-phase checker. Type, predicate and value sub-trees are constrained only structurally here and must validate independently against spec/type-expression.schema.json, spec/predicate-expression.schema.json and spec/value-expression.schema.json, exactly as spec/plan.schema.json handles its argument values.

type_address.description: A type artifact in the commons.

did.description: An agent identity: the Ed25519 public key that signs (spec/did-document.md).

signature.description: Ed25519 over the JCS-canonical record with only `signature` removed, so the signature covers the hash (the certification precedent, spec/certification.schema.json).

kebab_name.description: Lowercase kebab-case: need names, kinds, roles, ports, serving ids, resource classes.

snake_name.description: Attribute and field names, as spec/type-expression.schema.json spells record fields.

type_expression.description: A type-expression AST (spec/type-expression.schema.json); structural check only here.

predicate_expression.description: A predicate-expression AST (spec/predicate-expression.schema.json); structural check only here. Variables are the attribute names of the kind the predicate is over.

value_expression.description: A value-expression AST (spec/value-expression.schema.json); structural check only here.

world_state.description: The world-state vocabulary with the third built-in state this module proposes (design/proposals/01-ready-state.md): `ready` implies `exists`.

world_key_part.description: A key part of a resource named by a recipe step. Unlike a function record's own world refinements (keyed by its parameter names), a recipe step keys resources by the STEP'S bindings, so every key grounds at plan time from literals and instance names — names, not placeholders, keep plans literal.

oneOf.description: The step's positional argument, which must ground to a literal at plan time.
A top-level field of a JSON-bound argument (the REST creation idiom, spec/world-state.md).
One of the dish's name or placement inputs: a literal from the instance.
A name derived from one of the dish's name inputs by the recipe's fixed rule: also a literal from the instance.

A field of one of the dish's wire inputs. Grounds at plan time only when the producing recipe binds that output field from a plan-time binding (a resource NAME carried in the reference type); this is how a dish declares a dependency on another dish's resource, and why reference types carry names, not just links.

world_refinement.description: An authored requires/ensures on a recipe step (design/proposals/04-authored-refinements.md): the step's declared contract on the world, verified by test provisioning, consumed by the planner and by check-plan.

placement.description: Literal placement values for one serving: exactly the placement inputs its dish declares.

name_path.description: Where a name input sits in a serving's composition: component ids from the top-level dish down, ending in the name input's own name. `["name"]` is the top-level dish's input; `["net", "name"]` is component `net`'s.

serving_ref.description: A serving of an earlier receipt, by receipt address and serving id (decision 35).
